newsitem.title: INDIA: India privatisation panel seeks quick action.
newsitem.headline: India privatisation panel seeks quick action.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission said on Wednesday that it had urged the government to act fast to implement its recommendations on partial sale of government stakes in state companies.

"We have drawn the attention of the government to the fact that they (recommendations) have not been implemented," the commission's chairman, G.V. Ramakrishna, told a news conference after releasing the panel's fourth report.

The report recommended strategies to sell stakes in three companies, Hindustan Copper Ltd, Pawan Hans Helicopters Ltd and the Shipping Corp of India and advised the government against selling stakes in Power Grid Corp of India.
The government sold 19.88 percent of its shares in SCI in two tranches in 1992/93 (April-March) and 1993/94.

In its earlier three reports, the panel advised the government on 15 companies among which it recommended a partial sale of stakes in 12 companies, and deferred disinvestment in two companies after implementing some internal changes.
It recommended against disinvestment in one company.

On Wednesday, the commission said it wanted the government holding in SCI to fall below 51 percent through the sale of 30 percent of the total equity to five state-run oil refineries, who are key consumers of SCI's services.

It said the Indian Oil Corp, Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd, Bharat Petroleum Corp Ltd and Madras Refineries Ltd, Cochin Refineries Ltd could buy shares in the 30 percent stake in proportion to their net profits.

In addition, 10 percent could be offered to private and joint sector refineries, it said, adding this could pave the way for SCI to become an independent board-managed company outside government control.
"As a first step, the commission recommends that the board of SCI be broad-based by inducting a few non-executive directors from the relevant disciplines," it said.
The commission said Power Grid Corp, which runs power transmission lines, was involved in a core infrastructure area that needed further reforms and "proper commercial and market orientation."

Until this is achieved, Power Grid may not be able to attract the right kind of investor response and premature investment may result in considerable undervaluation of the shares of the company, the report said.
"The commission, therefore, recommends that disinvestment in Power Grid need not be considered for the time being," it said.

On Pawan Hans, in which the government owns 78.5 percent and the state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp the rest, the panel said ONGC should be given the first offer to buy out the government stake because it accounted for 85 percent of Pawan Hans' revenue.
"In the event that ONGC is not interested, the commission recommends that the government sells its entire holding of 78.5 percent to an investor," the report said.
The panel said Hindustan Copper Ltd was in the process of expanding a smelter and a mine project, cutting costs, reducing surplus staff and implementing a financial restructuring programme.
It recommended two alternative options for HCL.

Under the first, after effecting some key changes which may take two years to implement, HCL may select a strategic partner through a competitive bidding process to offer 51 percent of the company's equity, and sell 23 percent to employees, small investors and domestic institutions, the panel said.

Then other option would be to sell off 51 percent to a strategic partner at first and then implement a restructuring operation, after which the government could sell 23 percent to employees, small investors and institutions, the report said.
The commission's recommendation is not binding on the government.
